scenarios.name: Run to failure
scenarios.description: Nothing is serviced on condition: trucks are only ever repaired after they fail.

scenarios.name: Condition-based servicing
scenarios.description: Trucks come in when any component's wear reaches the threshold. Everything else is identical to the baseline.

scenarios.name: Servicing too early
scenarios.description: The same rule at a quarter of full wear. Fewer breakdowns, but the fleet spends its life in the workshop.

scenarios.name: Condition-based, worn trucks off mountain work
scenarios.description: Condition-based servicing plus a dispatch rule: a truck past a third of full wear is not sent on mountain routes.

scenarios.name: Condition-based, one bay
scenarios.description: Condition-based servicing with the second bay closed. Planned services and breakdown repairs compete for one bay.

scenarios.name: Condition-based, one part on the shelf
scenarios.description: Condition-based servicing with a single spare and a long parts lead time.

scenarios.name: Winter conditions
scenarios.description: Icy roads, slower speeds, more wear. Severity mean 1.4, speed mean 0.8.

scenarios.name: Summer baseline
scenarios.description: Dry roads, faster speeds. Severity mean 0.9, speed mean 1.1.

scenarios.name: Winter + demand surge
scenarios.description: The compound scenario: bad weather and high demand together.

scenarios.name: Route-aware dispatch + winter
scenarios.description: Tests whether the route restriction rule becomes more valuable in bad weather. Mountain wear limit 0.35, winter conditions.

metrics.name: Loads delivered on time
metrics.description: Loads that reached the customer inside the window.

metrics.name: Loads delivered late
metrics.description: Loads that arrived outside the window.

metrics.name: Loads dropped
metrics.description: Loads nobody collected plus loads lost to a breakdown.

metrics.name: Service level
metrics.description: Share of offered loads delivered on time.

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.description: Revenue from delivered loads. Late loads are paid at a discount.

metrics.name: Total fuel burned
metrics.code:
const fleet = state.places.Available.tokens.concat(state.places.OnRoute.tokens.concat(state.places.Returning.tokens.concat(state.places.DepotQueue.tokens.concat(state.places.InBay.tokens.concat(state.places.AwaitingParts.tokens.concat(state.places.Stranded.tokens.concat(state.places.UnderRecovery.tokens.concat(state.places.Rest.tokens))))))));
return fleet.reduce((total, truck) => total + truck.fuel_burned, 0);

metrics.name: Operating cost
metrics.description: Fuel cost plus repairs and services.

metrics.name: Profit
metrics.description: Revenue minus operating cost minus late delivery penalties.

metrics.name: Planned services
metrics.description: Trucks brought in on the wear rule and returned to as-new condition.

metrics.name: Services deferred
metrics.description: Times a truck was due for a service, found the workshop full.

metrics.name: Driver rest events
metrics.description: Times a truck was sent to mandatory rest.

metrics.name: Trucks earning
metrics.description: Trucks on a route right now.

metrics.name: Trucks off the road
metrics.description: Trucks in a bay, waiting for a part, under recovery, or resting.
metrics.code: return state.places.InBay.count + state.places.AwaitingParts.count + state.places.Stranded.count + state.places.UnderRecovery.count + state.places.Rest.count;
